resources.string: ZenMode OS uses this Accessibility Service for two things: to lock your screen when you tap the lock button on the home screen, and (only when you turn on in-app content blocking) to detect when a screen you chose to block (such as YouTube Shorts) is open, so it can navigate you away. It checks only which screen is showing; it does not read, store, or share the content itself, and does nothing for apps you have not chosen to block.

"%1$s uses Android's Accessibility Service API for two features:

1. Lock screen: Android gives a launcher no other way to lock the screen, so this permission is required for the lock button to work.

2. In-app content blocking (optional): when you turn on blocking for a surface such as YouTube Shorts, the service checks whether that screen is currently open and, if so, navigates you away. It runs only for apps you have explicitly chosen to block."

"• Uses the system lock-screen action (GLOBAL_ACTION_LOCK_SCREEN) when you tap the lock button\n• For apps you chose to block: checks which screen (view IDs) is visible and, on a blocked screen, presses Back\n• Only wakes for apps in your block list (currently YouTube)"
What this service does NOT do

"• Does NOT read, store, or transmit the text, media, or messages inside any app
• Does NOT monitor apps that are not in your block list
• Does NOT perform gestures or tap anything inside other apps
• Does NOT collect, store, transmit, or share any personal data
• Sends nothing off your device; all checks happen locally"

This service enables the lock button and, if you turn it on, in-app content blocking. It reads only which screen of a blocked app is visible, on the device, to decide whether to navigate away. No screen content or personal data is stored, collected, or sent anywhere.
